newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - US DATA, GERMAN RATES STEAL SPOTLIGHT.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - US DATA, GERMAN RATES STEAL SPOTLIGHT.

text.p: A wave of U.S. data including inflation and retail sales figures will flood financial markets this week, economists said.
In Europe the 'will they? won't they?' debate on German interest rates will dominate in the first part of the week, particularly if the mark continues to spiral down against the dollar.
Also on the agenda is the Bank of England's inflation report due on Wednesday, which is expected to bump gilts even higher with a benign outlook on inflation.

Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at Bank America in London, said there is a welter of U.S. data due out. ''With most people relatively comfortable that inflation in the U.S. is going to remain subdued for the time being, the focus there will be on the retail sales.''

He said there was some evidence consumption may have picked up a bit in July. "If we do see that, although no one is expecting the Fed to tighten policy in the near term, it will be enough to get people thinking about the possibility of the Fed raising before the end of the year," he said.
Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe also sounded a cautious note on retail sales.
"Three out of the four (data releases) will be okay, but retail sales are likely to come in quite strong...they will overshadow the week," he said.
"There will be confirmation from next week's numbers that third quarter growth looks to be picking up."
U.S. producer price data is due out on Wednesday as is July retail sales data, with consumer prices and industrial production data scheduled for release on Thursday.
Ken Wattret, international economist at Paribas in London, said the CPI and PPI would be the most significant for the Fed.
He expected only a modest month on month increase in CPI, giving a fall in the year on year rate.
"Against that background it's difficult to see the markets becoming concerned...so the fundamental background for Treasuries should be supportive," said Wattret.
In Germany and peripheral Europe, speculation over whether the Bundesbank will shift to a variable rate repo will dominate in the first part of the week, economists said.

"I don't think many people are expecting a change but there is certainly still a good deal of speculation they may decide to opt for additional variable rate repo on top of the fixed rate," said Hawkins.
"What they do come out with will be almost inevitably instrumental in shaping at least the near term outlook for the mark."
Watrett said a change in the Buba stance was unlikely.

"The most likely outcome is another set of fixed repos. Assuming the dollar doesn't rapidly gain momentum and threaten 2.0 to the mark, Buba will tolerate a temporary overshoot of the exchange rate," he said.
"But while the German interest rate outlook is unsure, it will have an adverse effect on southern Europe," he added.
Chester said the market would also be keeping half an eye on German retail sales data, expected some time during the week.
In Britain, the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report and minutes from the last monetary policy committee meeting are due for release on Wednesday.
Watrett said despite the boost to gilts after the latest interest rate rise and accompanying comments, the market may still find room for a further step up.
"To a certain extent the market has priced in (a benign inflation outlook) but there may still be a bit more mileage in some positive words in the report," he said.
Data-wise, UK producer prices are due on Monday, retail prices on Tuesday and unemployment and average earnings on Wednesday.
